newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Kok hopes for widest EMU membership from start.
newsitem.headline: Kok hopes for widest EMU membership from start.

text.p: Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok said the more countries that join the European single currency from the start, the better.
"The more members from the beginning, the better it will be," Kok told a news conference during a visit to Lisbon.
Kok was visiting Lisbon as part of preparations for a European Union summit in Amsterdam next month.
Kok said the Dutch, who currently holding the presidency of the European Union, were firmly against any sort of "pre-selection" over which member states would qualify for the single currency.
He said that he was convinced that come next spring, when European Union leaders decide which countries made the grade, the decision would be taken entirely on the basis of the entry criteria.
He said that he was equally convinced that there would be no delay to the launch of monetary union, due to come into force in January 1999.
"I am convinced that by the beginning of next year, when we come to make our decisions, the leading principles will be that we want to stick to the timetable and to the criteria," he said.
